Officer's narrative
Officers responded to a two-vehicle collision in Conroe, Texas, where a vehicle operated by Driver 1 and a vehicle
operated by Driver 2 came together head-on at low speed. Driver 1 reported neck pain consistent with whiplash, and
the injury described is a plausible result of an impact of this kind. Passenger was seated in the vehicle with Driver 1 at
the time of the collision, and both the responding officers and the scene itself confirm that Passenger was present.
Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the front ends of both vehicles that lines up with the reported point
of impact. No earlier damage to Driver 1's vehicle is known to officers or to either driver. No independent witnesses
came forward, so the account of the collision rests on the statements of the drivers and the physical evidence. Driver
1 is listed as a named driver on the insurance policy for the vehicle involved. Officers documented the scene,
collected the statements, and noted that the photographs corroborate several details of the drivers' accounts.
</page>

"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.

address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
